title: Chole Bhature
steps: Pressure cook soaked chickpeas with the tea bag/amla and salt until soft; discard tea bag.
Heat oil, saute onions till golden, add ginger-garlic paste and tomato puree, cook till oil separates.
Add chole masala powder, cooked chickpeas and a little cooking liquid; simmer 15 minutes.
For bhature, knead flour with yogurt, baking soda, a little oil and water into a soft dough; rest 2 hours.
Roll portions into ovals and deep fry in hot oil until puffed and golden on both sides.
Serve hot chole with bhature, sliced onions and pickle.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A tea bag simmered with the chickpeas gives the chole its classic dark colour without extra spices.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Resting the bhatura dough properly is what makes it puff up when fried.

title: Aloo Paratha
steps: Knead the atta with water and a little salt into a soft dough; rest 20 minutes.
Mix mashed potato with chilli, ajwain, chilli powder, coriander and salt for the stuffing.
Divide dough and stuffing into equal portions; stuff each dough ball with the potato mix.
Roll out gently into a paratha, being careful not to let the stuffing burst out.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee on both sides until golden-brown spots appear.
Serve hot with curd, butter and pickle.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Keep the stuffing dry, not wet, or the paratha will tear while rolling.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A dollop of white butter on top right before serving is the classic Punjabi touch.

title: Amritsari Kulcha
steps: Knead maida with yogurt, baking powder, salt and water into a soft dough; rest 1 hour.
Mix mashed potato with onion, ajwain, coriander and salt for the stuffing.
Stuff dough balls with the potato mixture and flatten gently into a round or oval shape.
Sprinkle kalonji on top and press lightly so the seeds stick.
Cook on a hot tawa or in a tandoor until browned and puffed, flipping to cook both sides.
Brush with butter and serve hot with chole and mint or tamarind chutney.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: In Chandigarh this is more often sold at dhabas as a chole-kulcha combo than made fresh at home.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A cast-iron tawa with a lid traps steam and helps the kulcha puff up without a tandoor.

title: Anda Bhurji (Egg Bhurji)
steps: Heat oil, saute onion and green chilli until soft.
Add tomato, turmeric and chilli powder; cook until the tomato softens.
Beat the eggs lightly with salt and pour into the pan.
Scramble continuously on medium heat until the eggs are just cooked through.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot with pav, roti or paratha.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Don't overcook the eggs — pull the pan off the heat while they still look slightly moist.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A pinch of garam masala at the end lifts the flavour.

title: Sarson da Saag with Makki di Roti
steps: Boil mustard leaves, spinach and bathua with ginger, garlic and green chilli until soft.
Blend coarsely (traditionally mashed by hand with a wooden madani) into a thick puree.
Return to the pan, whisk in makki atta to thicken, and simmer for 20-30 minutes.
In a separate pan, saute onion in ghee until golden and pour over the saag as a tempering (tadka).
For the roti, knead makki atta with warm water (it doesn't bind like wheat) and pat into small rounds.
Cook the roti on a hot tawa with ghee until browned on both sides, patching cracks with wet fingers as needed.
Serve saag topped with a knob of white butter alongside hot makki di roti.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: This is a winter-season dish across Punjab, Haryana and Himachal alike, so treat it as regional rather than uniquely Chandigarh's own.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Makki atta roti is fragile — pat it out directly on a damp cloth or plastic sheet instead of rolling with a pin.

title: Rajma Chawal
steps: Pressure cook the soaked rajma with salt and water until soft, about 6-7 whistles.
Heat oil, add cumin seeds, then onions and saute until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste, then tomato puree and cook until the oil separates.
Add chilli powder and garam masala, then the cooked rajma with its liquid.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes, lightly mashing a few beans to thicken the gravy.
Serve hot over steamed basmati rice.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Simmering longer after cooking deepens the flavour — many households make rajma a day ahead.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A splash of cream or a spoon of ghee at the end gives it a restaurant-style richness.

title: Kadhi Pakora
steps: Whisk yogurt with besan, turmeric and enough water to make a thin, smooth batter.
Make a separate thick besan batter with sliced onion and salt; deep fry spoonfuls into pakoras.
Heat oil, temper with mustard and cumin seeds, dried red chilli and ginger-garlic paste.
Pour in the yogurt-besan mixture, stirring continuously to prevent curdling; simmer 30-40 minutes.
Drop the fried pakoras into the simmering kadhi and cook another 10 minutes so they soften slightly.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Keep stirring while the kadhi comes to a boil the first time or the yogurt will split.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Punjabi kadhi is thicker than the Gujarati or Rajasthani versions — that's the regional giveaway.

title: Aloo Gobi
steps: Heat oil, add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add onions and ginger, saute until light golden.
Add turmeric, coriander powder and tomato; cook until soft.
Add potatoes and cauliflower, mix well, cover and cook on low heat until tender, stirring occasionally.
Uncover and cook a few minutes more so the vegetables dry out slightly and pick up a light char.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve with roti.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Cooking uncovered at the end gives the dry, slightly roasted texture that makes this dish distinctive.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Cut the cauliflower florets a bit larger than the potato cubes so both cook evenly.

title: Egg Curry (Anda Curry)
steps: Lightly slit the boiled eggs and shallow fry until the surface blisters slightly; set aside.
Heat oil, saute onions until golden, then add ginger-garlic paste.
Add tomato puree and all the dry spices; cook until the oil separates from the masala.
Add water to reach the desired gravy consistency and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the fried eggs, simmer for another 5 minutes so they soak up the gravy.
Finish with garam masala and coriander leaves; serve with rice or roti.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Slitting the eggs before frying helps the masala flavour seep in.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Frying the eggs first is optional but gives a nicer texture than dropping them in raw-boiled.

title: Punjabi Mutton Curry
steps: Marinate the mutton with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste and a little salt for at least 30 minutes.
Heat oil/ghee, temper with whole spices, then add onions and fry until deep golden-brown.
Add the marinated mutton and sear on high heat for a few minutes.
Add tomato puree and the dry spice powders; cook until the oil separates.
Add hot water to cover, cover the pan and simmer (or pressure cook) until the meat is tender.
Finish with garam masala, adjust the gravy consistency and simmer a final 5 minutes before serving with rice or roti.

fullIngredients.name: Whole spices (bay leaf, cloves, cinnamon, cardamom)

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Browning the onions well is the single biggest factor in the final colour and flavour of the gravy.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Bone-in cuts add more flavour to the gravy than boneless mutton.

title: Dal Makhani
steps: Pressure cook the soaked urad dal and rajma together with salt until very soft.
Heat butter, saute onions until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and cook a minute more.
Add tomato puree and spices; cook until the masala thickens and the oil separates.
Add the cooked dal and beans along with their liquid; simmer on low heat for at least 45 minutes, mashing lightly.
Stir in cream and a final knob of butter, then simmer 5 more minutes.
Serve hot with naan or steamed rice.

fullIngredients.name: Garam masala and red chilli powder

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The long, slow simmer is what develops the dish's signature creamy, smoky depth — don't rush it.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Restaurant versions credit the same Moti Mahal (Delhi) lineage as butter chicken, so it's shared North Indian heritage rather than a Chandigarh-specific invention.

title: Bhindi Masala
steps: Heat oil in a wide pan and fry the sliced okra on medium-high heat until lightly browned; remove and set aside.
In the same pan, saute onions until golden, then add tomato and cook until soft.
Add turmeric, coriander and chilli powder; cook the masala for a minute.
Return the fried okra to the pan, sprinkle amchur and salt, and toss gently to coat.
Cook uncovered for a few more minutes so the dish stays dry rather than gravy-like.
Serve with roti.

fullIngredients.name: Turmeric, coriander powder, red chilli powder

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Okra must be completely dry before cutting and frying, or it turns slimy.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Cooking it uncovered and not stirring too often helps it stay non-sticky.

title: Chana Masala
steps: Pressure cook the soaked chickpeas with salt until soft.
Heat oil, saute onions until golden-brown, then add ginger-garlic paste.
Add tomato puree and spices; cook until the oil separates from the masala.
Add the cooked chickpeas with some cooking liquid and simmer for 15-20 minutes.
Lightly mash a few chickpeas to thicken the gravy.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve with roti or rice.

fullIngredients.name: Chana masala or garam masala powder

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: This drier, home-style chana masala is distinct from the chole served with bhature, which is usually darker and tangier.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A squeeze of lemon just before serving brightens the dish.

title: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
steps: Marinate chicken pieces in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder and salt for at least 1 hour.
Grill, roast or pan-sear the marinated chicken until cooked through and lightly charred; set aside.
Heat butter in a pan, add tomato puree and simmer until it thickens and darkens slightly.
Stir in cashew paste or cream to make the gravy smooth and rich.
Add the cooked chicken pieces and simmer for 10 minutes so they soak up the gravy.
Finish with crushed kasuri methi and a final swirl of butter; serve with naan or rice.

fullIngredients.name: Tandoori masala or red chilli powder

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: This dish traces back to the Moti Mahal restaurant lineage in 1950s Delhi, popularised by Punjabi refugee chefs — it's shared North Indian/Punjabi heritage rather than something unique to Chandigarh.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Cashew paste gives a similar richness to cream with a slightly nuttier finish.

title: Tandoori Chicken
steps: Score the chicken pieces and marinate first with lemon juice and salt for 15 minutes.
Mix yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, tandoori masala, chilli powder and mustard oil; coat the chicken well.
Marinate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight, in the refrigerator.
Roast in a tandoor, on a grill or in a hot oven, basting occasionally, until charred and cooked through.
Rest for a few minutes, then serve with mint chutney, sliced onions and lemon wedges.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Scoring the meat before marinating helps the masala penetrate deeper.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A high oven temperature (240°C+) with a final broil gives the closest result to a real tandoor char at home.

title: Samosa
steps: Knead maida with ajwain, salt, a little oil and water into a firm dough; rest 20 minutes.
Heat oil, temper cumin seeds, add ginger and green chilli, then peas and potatoes.
Add the spice powders and salt, mash lightly and cook for a few minutes; cool the filling.
Roll the dough into ovals, cut in half, and shape each half into a cone.
Fill the cone with the potato mixture, seal the edges with a little water.
Deep fry on low-medium heat until golden and crisp all over.
Serve hot with tamarind and mint chutney.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Frying on low heat first keeps the samosa from browning before the inside layers are cooked through.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Sealing the edges firmly prevents the filling from leaking out into the oil.

title: Pyaaz Pakora (Onion Fritters)
steps: Mix sliced onions with salt and let them sit for 10 minutes to release moisture.
Add besan, rice flour, chilli powder, turmeric, ajwain and coriander leaves; mix without adding extra water.
The onion's released moisture should be enough to bind a thick, clumpy batter.
Heat oil and drop small clusters of the mixture in; fry until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with green chutney and masala chai.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Resist adding water — the salted onions release enough liquid on their own for a crisper fritter.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: This is a rainy-season and evening tea-time favourite across most of North India, not something exclusive to the Chandigarh region.

title: Chicken Malai Tikka
steps: Mix hung curd, cream, ginger-garlic paste, green chilli paste, cheese and garam masala into a smooth marinade.
Coat the chicken cubes well and marinate for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.
Skewer the chicken pieces and grill, roast or pan-sear until lightly charred and cooked through.
Baste with ghee or oil once or twice while cooking to keep the chicken moist.
Serve hot with mint chutney, onion rings and lemon wedges.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The cream and cheese give this tikka its pale colour and mild, creamy flavour, unlike the redder, spicier standard chicken tikka.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Don't over-marinate beyond 24 hours — the dairy can start to break down the chicken's texture.
